name: Nyungwe Forest National Park
blurb: Montane rainforest of monkeys, chimpanzees and forest cats in the Albertine Rift.

tip.title: Thin out the colobus
tip.text: Angola colobus are leaf eaters and prey for chimpanzees, leopards and crowned eagles. Set them to -100% and watch the predators that rely on monkeys.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Light reaching the forest floor is limited by the dense canopy, so gaps and edges are where much of the undergrowth grows.

nodes.name: Rain and mist
nodes.desc: Moist montane air and regular rainfall keep this rainforest, bog and bamboo mosaic green.

nodes.name: Forest soil
nodes.desc: Leaf litter and dead wood are turned into soil nutrients that the forest plants draw on again.

nodes.name: Fungi and bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, dead wood and dead animals, returning nutrients to the soil.

nodes.name: Galiniera
nodes.desc: A montane shrub or small tree whose fruit is eaten by blue monkeys and several forest birds in recorded observations.

nodes.name: Lantana
nodes.desc: A flowering shrub of forest edges, introduced to Africa. Its berries are eaten by monkeys, bats and birds, and its flowers attract butterflies.

nodes.name: Giant lobelia
nodes.desc: A tall flowering Afromontane lobelia of the Albertine Rift highlands, whose nectar-rich flowers suit sunbirds.

nodes.name: Angola colobus
nodes.desc: Leaf-eating monkey that also takes some fruit and seeds. Nyungwe is noted for unusually large groups.

nodes.name: L'Hoest's monkey
nodes.desc: Mostly plant eater of fruit, leaves, roots and mushrooms, occasionally eggs and small animals. Favours dense undergrowth in mountain forest.

nodes.name: Blue monkey
nodes.desc: A forest guenon that has been recorded eating fruit from Galiniera and Lantana.

nodes.name: Great blue turaco
nodes.desc: A large fruit-eating forest bird, recorded feeding on Galiniera fruit.

nodes.name: Common bulbul
nodes.desc: An abundant, fruit-eating songbird recorded taking Galiniera and Lantana fruit.

nodes.name: Regal sunbird
nodes.desc: An Albertine Rift endemic sunbird that feeds on nectar from montane flowers.

nodes.name: Temminck's mouse
nodes.desc: A small African rodent of grassy and bushy habitats; prey for the Great Lakes bush viper.

nodes.name: Acraea butterflies
nodes.desc: A large genus of butterflies, many species recorded in the Nyungwe area. Adults visit flowers for nectar.

nodes.name: Chimpanzee
nodes.desc: Eats mainly fruit but also hunts monkeys and other small mammals. Nyungwe holds chimpanzee communities.

nodes.name: Great Lakes bush viper
nodes.desc: A tree-dwelling viper of Albertine Rift forests, recorded eating Temminck's mouse.

nodes.name: Johnston's chameleon
nodes.desc: A three-horned montane chameleon of the Albertine Rift that catches insects.

nodes.name: African paradise flycatcher
nodes.desc: Insect-catching forest bird, also recorded taking Lantana fruit.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: Top carnivore of African forests, taking medium-sized prey such as monkeys and duikers; known to prey on chimpanzees in some areas.

nodes.name: African golden cat
nodes.desc: Secretive forest cat eating mainly rodents and tree hyrax, plus birds and small monkeys.

nodes.name: Crowned eagle
nodes.desc: Forest eagle whose main prey is monkeys, including colobus and blue monkeys, along with small antelopes.
